# Remove-ZbxMaintenance

## SYNOPSIS

Removes maintenance periods.

## SYNTAX

```
Remove-ZbxMaintenance [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixMaintenanceRecord>[]> [-Force] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A maintenance period suppresses problems, and optionally data collection, for hosts and host groups during planned work. The Remove-ZbxMaintenance cmdlet deletes the maintenance periods given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with maintenance.delete, all in one call when the pipeline ends. It asks for confirmation first unless -Confirm:$false or -Force is given, and -WhatIf lists what would be deleted. It writes nothing, and needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Delete a maintenance by name

```powershell
Remove-ZbxMaintenance -InputObject 'Patch window' -Confirm:$false
```

-InputObject takes a name, an id or a maintenance object. ConfirmImpact is High, so PowerShell asks first unless -Confirm:$false is given. The hosts leave maintenance at once.

### Example 2: Delete every expired maintenance, through the pipeline

```powershell
$now = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow
Get-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Patch*' | Where-Object ActiveTill -LT $now | Remove-ZbxMaintenance -WhatIf
Get-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Patch*' | Where-Object ActiveTill -LT $now | Remove-ZbxMaintenance -Confirm:$false
Get-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Patch*' -CountOutput
```

Get-ZbxMaintenance writes maintenance objects; the ones whose ActiveTill has passed are piped to Remove-ZbxMaintenance, which deletes them in one call. Run it with -WhatIf first to see what would go.
